title: Prediction with Expert Advice under Heavy-Tailed Losses
abstract: arXiv:2610.14904v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We study prediction with expert advice over $T$ rounds with $K$ experts under heavy-tailed losses whose $(1+\epsilon)$-moment is bounded by $\theta>0$ for some $\epsilon\in(0,1]$. In this setting, existing algorithms designed for the case $\epsilon=1$ can be suboptimal when $\epsilon<1$, suffering an additional polynomial dependence on $K$. We characterize the minimax pseudo-regret rate as $\Theta((\theta T)^{\frac{1}{1+\epsilon}}(\log K)^{\frac{\epsilon}{1+\epsilon}})$ and establish gap-dependent lower bounds in a self-bounded environment. To attain this minimax rate without prior knowledge of either $\epsilon$ or $\theta$, we propose Adaptive Heavy-Tailed FTRL, which uses robust data-dependent scale adaptation together with truncation. We further develop Adaptive Heavy-Tailed OMD, which likewise requires neither $\epsilon$ nor $\theta$ and achieves near-optimal regret guarantees in both adversarial and self-bounded environments. Fina

translated_title: 重尾损失下的专家建议预测
translated_abstract: 我们研究在重尾损失下、经过 $T$ 轮且有 $K$ 个专家的专家建议预测问题，其中重尾损失的 $(1+\epsilon)$ 阶矩被 $\theta>0$ 所界定，$\epsilon\in(0,1]$。在这一设定下，为 $\epsilon=1$ 情形设计的现有算法在 $\epsilon<1$ 时可能是次优的，会额外产生对 $K$ 的多项式依赖。我们将极小极大伪遗憾率刻画为 $\Theta((\theta T)^{\frac{1}{1+\epsilon}}(\log K)^{\frac{\epsilon}{1+\epsilon}})$，并在自受限环境中建立了依赖于间隙的下界。为了在无需预知 $\epsilon$ 或 $\theta$ 的情况下达到该极小极大率，我们提出了自适应重尾 FTRL（Adaptive Heavy-Tailed FTRL），它使用鲁棒的数据依赖尺度自适应并结合截断技术。我们进一步发展了自适应重尾 OMD（Adaptive Heavy-Tailed OMD），它同样既不需要 $\epsilon$ 也不需要 $\theta$，并且在对抗性环境和自受限环境中都能实现近乎最优的遗憾保证。
tldr: 本文针对重尾损失下的专家建议预测问题刻画了极小极大伪遗憾率，并提出无需预知矩参数 ε 和 θ 的自适应重尾 FTRL 与 OMD 算法，在对抗性和自受限环境中均实现近乎最优的遗憾保证。
en_tdlr: This paper characterizes the minimax pseudo-regret rate for prediction with expert advice under heavy-tailed losses and proposes Adaptive Heavy-Tailed FTRL and OMD algorithms that achieve near-optimal regret guarantees in both adversarial and self-bounded environments without prior knowledge of the moment parameters ε and θ.
